question: Does rustc codegen (opt-level / codegen-units / LTO) materially move the Detcore deterministic-mode per-syscall coordinator-RPC floor (~13.6us/syscall) that dominates all backends?
answer: NO. The floor is ~65.5% system/kernel time (pidfd_open/clock_nanosleep/openat scheduling + IPC, busy-poll) and only ~34.5% user-space CPU (median K=2 anchor, sched_yield). Hermit/detcore is ALREADY built at opt-level=3; the untried levers are measured-inert: codegen-units=1 = +2.2% (noise, inguest-handler study) and LTO = <=2% runtime + net compile loss with 83% supervisor CPU in kernel (ci-build-profile-lto study, same day). Best-case whole-floor improvement ~0.35*~5% ~= 2%, within noise. Real lever = eliminate the per-syscall coordinator round-trip (in-process/shared-mem fastpath, in-guest RCB via rdpmc).
method: Median-of-5 CPU-time (user+sys) + wall slope across well-separated N (10000->50000) under `hermit run --backend liteinst` (deterministic by default), boxed via scratch/run-on-k-free-cores.py; /usr/bin/time -v. K=2 (coordinator RPC LIVELOCKS at K=1 -- it is a 2-thread guest<->coordinator ping-pong, not single-threaded; that livelock is itself proof of IPC/scheduling-bound cost). Absolute us are load-inflated on shared host; only the ~35/65 user:sys RATIO is relied upon (reproduced across 5 cells).
